scenes.title: Loving and the Friend
scenes.summary: Loving is wishing for someone what one thinks good, for his sake and not one's own, and being disposed to bring it about; a friend loves and is loved in return, shares one's joys and pains, and has the same friends and enemies.

scenes.title: Whom People Love
scenes.summary: People love their benefactors and those who would benefit them, the friends of their friends, the generous, the brave and the just, the self-controlled, those pleasant to live with who can take a joke, those who praise them and bear no grudges, those like them, unless they compete for a living, “potter against potter”, and those before whom they need feel no shame.

scenes.title: Kinds and Causes of Friendship
scenes.summary: The kinds of friendship are comradeship, intimacy and kinship; what produces it is a favor, done unasked and without display.

scenes.title: Enmity and Hatred
scenes.summary: Enmity comes from anger, spite and slander; unlike anger, hatred needs no injury to oneself, is felt toward classes, is incurable, wants harm rather than pain, is itself painless and wishes its object not to exist. So the speaker can show, make or break friendships and enmities.
